scenes.heading: Reaction pathways
scenes.sub: Plan the route from start to target
scenes.say: A reaction pathway is a planned series of reactions that turns a starting material into a target molecule, one functional group at a time. It's how chemists make medicines, plastics and flavours.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Bus, then train, then tram: one leg at a time to the footy
scenes.science: Each step changes one functional group on the way to the target
scenes.breaks: transport runs both ways, but not every reaction can be reversed, and the chain usually stays the same length.
scenes.say: Getting to the footy might take a bus, a train, then a tram. A pathway is the same: one step at a time, each changing one functional group. Alkenes and alcohols are the big interchange stations, where many lines meet.

scenes.heading: Learn the map
scenes.say: Learn the map. Alkenes become alcohols with steam and a phosphoric acid catalyst. Haloalkanes become alcohols with sodium hydroxide. Primary alcohols oxidise to carboxylic acids, and secondary alcohols to ketones. And an acid plus an alcohol gives an ester.

scenes.heading: Designing a pathway
steps: Count carbons in start and target
scenes.say: To design a pathway, count the carbons. More carbons in the target usually means two pieces joined by condensation. Then work backwards: what could this be made from in one step? Choose reagents, and check each group is on the right carbon.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Design a pathway from ethene to ethyl ethanoate, CH₃COOCH₂CH₃.
lines: 3: acid + ethanol, conc. H₂SO₄ → ethyl ethanoate
scenes.say: Work backwards. The ester comes from ethanoic acid and ethanol, and both have two carbons. Hydrate ethene to make ethanol. Oxidise some of it to ethanoic acid. Then react the acid with the rest of the ethanol, using concentrated sulfuric acid.

scenes.heading: Overall yield
scenes.say: Every step loses some product, so multiply the step yields as decimals. Three steps at eighty percent each give only fifty-one point two percent overall. Fewer steps means more product.
scenes.caption: Every step loses some product, so multiply the step yields as decimals. Three steps at 80% each give only 51.2% overall. Fewer steps means more product.

scenes.heading: Green chemistry
scenes.say: Green chemistry favours fewer steps, high atom economy, catalysts, renewable feedstocks like ethanol from fermented sugar, less energy, and safer reagents, avoiding toxic chromium six compounds. When comparing pathways, name the principle and the specific evidence.
scenes.caption: Green chemistry favours fewer steps, high atom economy, catalysts, renewable feedstocks like ethanol from fermented sugar, less energy, and safer reagents, avoiding toxic chromium(VI) compounds. When comparing pathways, name the principle and the specific evidence.

points: Alkenes and alcohols are the hubs
scenes.say: Quick recap. Alkenes and alcohols are the hubs. Work backwards and check every position. Multiply yields, never average them. And greener pathways use fewer steps, catalysts and renewable feedstocks. Now try the practice questions!
